summary: Steel state fire tower on headquarters hill at Camp Upton, Suffolk County, completed January 1932; closed 1953, removed 1955 or 1956; site now Brookhaven National Laboratory.

facts.design: Steel fire observation tower; the register names an Aermotor LS-40 with wood steps and landing platforms
facts.status_note: Removed in 1955 or 1956; the Long Island list says concrete footers still remain at the north site

events.note: A May 1931 item announced a 70-foot steel tower for the heights at Camp Upton
A June 1931 item said the tower would be erected east of Yaphank; a State Ranger found the Selden and Flanders towers inadequate
Completed January 1932 on headquarters hill; 70 feet per the 1932 report, 60 feet per the Long Island list for the north site
The 1932 report said a man would be kept on duty March 15 to November 15 (planned)
Closed in 1953 (register and Long Island list)
Register says the state removed it in 1955; the Long Island list says Brookhaven National Laboratory removed the towers in 1955 or 1956

corrections.why: The 1931 and 1932 items describe a steel fire observation tower on headquarters hill; no source read describes a rooftop structure.

notes_for_editor: This record (40.87049, -72.87596) is labelled Rooftop on the Forest Fire Lookout Association county list. It is about 1.3 km from the North site record (40.87744, -72.86374) and about 0.8 km from the South site (40.86657, -72.86804), so it may duplicate us-ny-camp-upton-north or be a separate point; the editor should decide. The story follows the 1931-32 reports of a steel tower on headquarters hill, which the North register also describes. Sources disagree on height (70 ft in the 1932 report, 60 ft in the Long Island list for the north site) and on removal (state in 1955 per the register; Brookhaven in 1955 or 1956 per the Long Island list). The footers statement refers to the north site. No source read says anything about access, so facts.access is omitted. Staffing is a 1932 plan, so no staffing facts are recorded. The brief's kind 'rooftop' is proposed for correction; no source read supports it. Two of the three cited pages are newspaper transcriptions.
